+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Generates the quantization reference tables for the docs.
+
+Like `generate_attention_backends.py`, this parses source with `ast` instead of
+importing it, so the docs build does not need CUDA, ROCm, or `torch`.
+
+Only registries written as literals are read: method, shorthand and scheme
+names, the per-platform allow-lists, and the linear kernel registries.
+Whether a kernel runs on a device is decided by code (`is_supported`,
+`can_implement`) and is deliberately not rendered.
+
+Adding an entry to a registry must never require an edit here: a value this
+script does not recognize is rendered as written in the source. The build fails
+only when a registry it looks up by name is missing or is no longer a literal.
+"""
+
+import ast
+import logging
+import sys
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
+
+from generated_content import fill_markers  # noqa: E402
+
+logger = logging.getLogger("mkdocs")
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent.parent
+VLLM_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "vllm"
+QUANT_DIR = VLLM_DIR / "model_executor" / "layers" / "quantization"
+
+QUANT_CONFIG_FILE = VLLM_DIR / "config" / "quantization.py"
+QUANT_UTILS_FILE = QUANT_DIR / "utils" / "quant_utils.py"

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# AST helpers
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+class Source:
+    """One parsed source file, with errors that name it."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
+        self.path = path
+        self.tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(), filename=str(path))
+        self.assigned = _assignments(self.tree.body)
+
+    def error(self, message: str) -> ValueError:
+        rel = self.path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT).as_posix()
+        return ValueError(f"{rel}: {message}; update {Path(__file__).name}")
+
+    def require(self, name: str) -> ast.expr:
+        if name not in self.assigned:
+            raise self.error(f"{name} not found")
+        return self.assigned[name]
+
+    def dict_items(self, name: str, node: ast.expr) -> Iterator[tuple[str, ast.expr]]:
+        """Items of a dict literal with string keys."""
+        if not isinstance(node, ast.Dict):
+            raise self.error(f"{name} is not a dict literal")
+        for key, value in zip(node.keys, node.values, strict=True):
+            if not (isinstance(key, ast.Constant) and isinstance(key.value, str)):
+                raise self.error(f"{name} has a key that is not a string literal")
+            yield key.value, value
+
+    def strings(self, name: str, node: ast.expr) -> list[str]:
+        """A list, tuple or set literal of strings, optionally wrapped in a call
+        such as `frozenset(...)`."""
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and len(node.args) == 1 and not node.keywords:
+            node = node.args[0]
+        if isinstance(node, ast.List | ast.Tuple | ast.Set):
+            values = [e.value for e in node.elts if isinstance(e, ast.Constant)]
+            if len(values) == len(node.elts) and all(
+                isinstance(value, str) for value in values
+            ):
+                return values
+        raise self.error(f"{name} is not a literal collection of strings")
+
+    def elements(self, name: str, node: ast.expr) -> list[str]:
+        """Names of the classes in a list, tuple or set literal."""
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and not node.args and not node.keywords:
+            return []
+        if not isinstance(node, ast.List | ast.Tuple | ast.Set) or any(
+            isinstance(element, ast.Starred) for element in node.elts
+        ):
+            raise self.error(f"{name} is not a literal collection")
+        return [_short(element) for element in node.elts]
+
+
+def _assignments(body: list[ast.stmt]) -> dict[str, ast.expr]:
+    """Map names to their assigned expression. The last assignment wins, as it
+    does at runtime."""
+    assigned: dict[str, ast.expr] = {}
+    for node in body:
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and len(node.targets) == 1:
+            target, value = node.targets[0], node.value
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.AnnAssign) and node.value is not None:
+            target, value = node.target, node.value
+        else:
+            continue
+        if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
+            assigned[target.id] = value
+    return assigned
+
+
+def _short(node: ast.expr) -> str:
+    """An expression as written, without the module prefix of a name."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, str):
+        return node.value
+    return node.attr if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) else ast.unparse(node)
+
+
+def _as_call(node: ast.expr | None, name: str) -> ast.Call | None:
+    """`node` if it is a call to `name`, as `name(...)` or `module.name(...)`."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and _short(node.func) == name:
+        return node
+    return None
+
+
+def _call_args(call: ast.Call, params: tuple[str, ...]) -> dict[str, ast.expr]:
+    """Bind positional and keyword arguments of `call` to `params`."""
+    bound = dict(zip(params, call.args))
+    bound.update({kw.arg: kw.value for kw in call.keywords if kw.arg})
+    return bound
+
+
+def _is_none(node: ast.expr | None) -> bool:
+    return node is None or (isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and node.value is None)
+
+
+def _code(text: str) -> str:
+    return f"`{text}`"
+
+
+def _table(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:
+    lines = [header, ["---"] * len(header), *rows]
+    return "\n".join(
+        "| " + " | ".join(cell.replace("|", "\\|") for cell in cells) + " |"
+        for cells in lines
+    )
+
+
+def _platform_sort_key(platform: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
+    if platform in PLATFORM_ORDER:
+        return PLATFORM_ORDER.index(platform), ""
+    return len(PLATFORM_ORDER), platform
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Quantization keys
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ScaleSpec:
+    """A parsed `ScaleDesc`. `dtype` is the source expression."""
+
+    dtype: str
+    static: bool
+    group: tuple[int, int]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class QuantKeySpec:
+    """A parsed `QuantKey`. `dtype` is the source expression."""
+
+    dtype: str
+    scale: ScaleSpec
+    scale2: ScaleSpec | None
+    symmetric: bool
+
+
+class QuantKeys:
+    """Resolves the module-level `QuantKey` assignments of `quant_utils.py`."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        source = Source(QUANT_UTILS_FILE)
+        self._assigned = source.assigned
+        # `GroupShape.PER_TENSOR = GroupShape(-1, -1)` and friends.
+        self._group_aliases: dict[str, ast.expr] = {}
+        for node in source.tree.body:
+            if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and len(node.targets) == 1:
+                target = node.targets[0]
+                if (
+                    isinstance(target, ast.Attribute)
+                    and ast.unparse(target.value) == "GroupShape"
+                ):
+                    self._group_aliases[target.attr] = node.value
+
+    def resolve(self, node: ast.expr) -> QuantKeySpec | None:
+        """Parse a reference to a `QuantKey`, or return None for one that is not
+        written as a literal `QuantKey(...)` in `quant_utils.py`."""
+        try:
+            call = _as_call(self._deref(node), "QuantKey")
+            if call is None:
+                return None
+            args = _call_args(call, ("dtype", "scale", "scale2", "symmetric"))
+            scale2, symmetric = args.get("scale2"), args.get("symmetric")
+            return QuantKeySpec(
+                dtype=ast.unparse(args["dtype"]),
+                scale=self._scale(args["scale"]),
+                scale2=None if _is_none(scale2) else self._scale(scale2),
+                symmetric=_is_none(symmetric) or bool(ast.literal_eval(symmetric)),
+            )
+        except (KeyError, ValueError):
+            return None
+
+    def _deref(self, node: ast.expr) -> ast.expr:
+        for _ in range(len(self._assigned) + 1):
+            name = _short(node)
+            if isinstance(node, ast.Call) or name not in self._assigned:
+                break
+            node = self._assigned[name]
+        return node
+
+    def _scale(self, node: ast.expr | None) -> ScaleSpec:
+        call = None if node is None else _as_call(self._deref(node), "ScaleDesc")
+        if call is None:
+            raise ValueError("not a ScaleDesc literal")
+        args = _call_args(call, ("dtype", "static", "group_shape"))
+        return ScaleSpec(
+            dtype=ast.unparse(args["dtype"]),
+            static=bool(ast.literal_eval(args["static"])),
+            group=self._group(args["group_shape"]),
+        )
+
+    def _group(self, node: ast.expr) -> tuple[int, int]:
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and node.attr in self._group_aliases:
+            node = self._group_aliases[node.attr]
+        call = _as_call(self._deref(node), "GroupShape")
+        if call is None:
+            raise ValueError("not a GroupShape literal")
+        args = _call_args(call, ("row", "col"))
+        return int(ast.literal_eval(args["row"])), int(ast.literal_eval(args["col"]))
+
+
+def _dtype_name(expr: str, names: dict[str, str]) -> str:
+    return names.get(expr) or _code(expr.rsplit(".", 1)[-1])
+
+
+def _shared_by(scale: ScaleSpec) -> str:
+    """What shares one scale value."""
+    row, col = scale.group
+    if (row, col) == (-1, -1):
+        return "tensor"
+    if (row, col) == (-1, 1):
+        return "output channel"
+    if (row, col) == (1, -1):
+        return "row" if scale.static else "token"
+    if row == 1 and col > 0:
+        return f"{col} elements"
+    return f"{row}×{col} block"
+
+
+def _scale_text(scale: ScaleSpec) -> str:
+    return f"{_dtype_name(scale.dtype, SCALE_DTYPE_NAMES)} per {_shared_by(scale)}"
+
+
+def _data_text(key: QuantKeySpec) -> str:
+    text = _dtype_name(key.dtype, DATA_DTYPE_NAMES)
+    return text if key.symmetric else f"{text}, asymmetric"
+
+
+def _key_text(key: QuantKeySpec) -> str:
+    """One-line description of a key that has no name of its own."""
+    parts = [_data_text(key), _scale_text(key.scale)]
+    if key.scale2 is not None:
+        parts.append(_scale_text(key.scale2))
+    return ", ".join(parts)
+
+
+def _computed(scale: ScaleSpec) -> str:
+    return "at load" if scale.static else "per forward pass"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Scheme:
+    """A name accepted on the `weight` and `activation` fields."""
+
+    name: str
+    source: str
+    key: QuantKeySpec | None
+    # Key used instead when the name is given as a weight.
+    weight_key: QuantKeySpec | None
+    # Layer kinds with an online method that quantizes weights to this scheme.
+    online: list[str]
+
+
+def _online_weight_kinds(keys: QuantKeys) -> dict[QuantKeySpec, list[str]]:
+    source = Source(ONLINE_METHODS_FILE)
+    kinds: dict[QuantKeySpec, list[str]] = {}
+    for registry, kind in (
+        ("_ONLINE_LINEAR_METHODS", "linear"),
+        ("_ONLINE_MOE_METHODS", "MoE"),
+    ):
+        table = source.require(registry)
+        if not isinstance(table, ast.Dict):
+            raise source.error(f"{registry} is not a dict literal")
+        for key_node, method in zip(table.keys, table.values, strict=True):
+            key = None if key_node is None else keys.resolve(key_node)
+            if key is None:
+                continue
+            # Methods for the lm_head are registered with the linear ones.
+            is_lm_head = "lmhead" in _short(method).lower()
+            kinds.setdefault(key, []).append("lm_head" if is_lm_head else kind)
+    return kinds
+
+
+def parse_schemes(keys: QuantKeys) -> list[Scheme]:
+    source = Source(QUANT_CONFIG_FILE)
+    weight_names = dict(
+        source.dict_items(
+            "_WEIGHT_QUANT_KEY_NAMES", source.require("_WEIGHT_QUANT_KEY_NAMES")
+        )
+    )
+    online = _online_weight_kinds(keys)
+    schemes = []
+    for name, node in source.dict_items(
+        "QUANT_KEY_NAMES", source.require("QUANT_KEY_NAMES")
+    ):
+        key = keys.resolve(node)
+        weight_key = keys.resolve(weight_names[name]) if name in weight_names else None
+        as_weight = weight_key or key
+        schemes.append(
+            Scheme(
+                name=name,
+                source=_short(node),
+                key=key,
+                weight_key=weight_key,
+                online=online.get(as_weight, []) if as_weight else [],
+            )
+        )
+    if schemes and not any(scheme.key for scheme in schemes):
+        raise Source(QUANT_UTILS_FILE).error(
+            "no QUANT_KEY_NAMES entry resolves to a QuantKey(dtype, scale, scale2, "
+            "symmetric) of ScaleDesc(dtype, static, group_shape)"
+        )
+    return schemes
+
+
+def render_schemes(schemes: list[Scheme]) -> str:
+    rows = []
+    for scheme in schemes:
+        key = scheme.key
+        if key is None:
+            rows.append([_code(scheme.name), _code(scheme.source), "–", "–", "–"])
+            continue
+        if scheme.weight_key is None:
+            computed = _computed(key.scale)
+        else:
+            computed = (
+                f"{_computed(scheme.weight_key.scale)} (weight), "
+                f"{_computed(key.scale)} (activation)"
+            )
+        scale = _scale_text(key.scale)
+        if key.scale2 is not None:
+            scale += f", then {_scale_text(key.scale2)} ({_computed(key.scale2)})"
+        rows.append(
+            [
+                _code(scheme.name),
+                _data_text(key),
+                scale,
+                computed,
+                ", ".join(scheme.online) or "–",
+            ]
+        )
+    return _table(
+        ["Name", "Data", "Scale", "Scale computed", "Online weight for"], rows
+    )
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# `--quantization` values
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def parse_platform_allow_lists() -> dict[str, set[str] | None]:
+    """The `--quantization` values each platform accepts.
+
+    None is a platform without a `supported_quantization` list, which accepts
+    every value.
+    """
+    interface = PLATFORMS_DIR / "interface.py"
+    allow_lists: dict[str, set[str] | None] = {}
+    found_default = False
+    for path in sorted(PLATFORMS_DIR.glob("*.py")):
+        source = Source(path)
+        for cls in source.tree.body:
+            if not isinstance(cls, ast.ClassDef):
+                continue
+            assigned = _assignments(cls.body)
+            allowed = assigned.get("supported_quantization")
+            if path == interface:
+                found_default |= allowed is not None
+                continue
+            if isinstance(allowed, ast.List) and not allowed.elts:
+                allowed = None
+            if allowed is None and "_enum" not in assigned:
+                continue
+            name = cls.name.removesuffix("Platform")
+            if "_enum" in assigned:
+                enum = _short(assigned["_enum"])
+                name = PLATFORM_NAMES.get(enum, enum)
+            allow_lists[name] = (
+                None
+                if allowed is None
+                else set(source.strings(f"{cls.name}.supported_quantization", allowed))
+            )
+    if not found_default:
+        raise Source(interface).error("Platform.supported_quantization not found")
+    return dict(sorted(allow_lists.items(), key=lambda i: _platform_sort_key(i[0])))
+
+
+def _accepted_on(names: list[str], allow_lists: dict[str, set[str] | None]) -> str:
+    """Platforms that accept at least one of `names`."""
+    platforms = [
+        platform
+        for platform, allowed in allow_lists.items()
+        if allowed is None or allowed.intersection(names)
+    ]
+    return ", ".join(platforms) or "–"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class LayerSpec:
+    """The `QuantSpec` of an online shorthand. `weight` is None when the weight
+    is not a named `QuantKey` literal; `weight_source` is then shown instead."""
+
+    weight: QuantKeySpec | None
+    weight_source: str
+    hadamard_size: str | None
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Shorthand:
+    name: str
+    linear: LayerSpec | None
+    moe: LayerSpec | None
+    # Also a checkpoint method name.
+    deferred: bool
+
+
+def parse_shorthands(keys: QuantKeys) -> list[Shorthand]:
+    source = Source(QUANT_CONFIG_FILE)
+    deferred = source.strings(
+        "_DEFERRED_ONLINE_SHORTHANDS", source.require("_DEFERRED_ONLINE_SHORTHANDS")
+    )
+
+    def layer_spec(node: ast.expr | None) -> LayerSpec | None:
+        if node is None or _is_none(node):
+            return None
+        call = _as_call(node, "QuantSpec")
+        if call is None:
+            return LayerSpec(None, _short(node), None)
+        args = _call_args(call, ("weight", "activation", "hadamard_size"))
+        weight, hadamard = args.get("weight"), args.get("hadamard_size")
+        if weight is None or _is_none(weight):
+            return None
+        return LayerSpec(
+            weight=keys.resolve(weight),
+            weight_source=_short(weight),
+            hadamard_size=None if _is_none(hadamard) else ast.unparse(hadamard),
+        )
+
+    shorthands = []
+    for name, value in source.dict_items(
+        "_ONLINE_SHORTHANDS", source.require("_ONLINE_SHORTHANDS")
+    ):
+        call = _as_call(value, "QuantizationConfigArgs")
+        if call is None or any(kw.arg is None for kw in call.keywords):
+            raise source.error(
+                f"_ONLINE_SHORTHANDS[{name!r}] is not a literal "
+                "QuantizationConfigArgs(...)"
+            )
+        args = _call_args(call, ("linear", "moe"))
+        shorthands.append(
+            Shorthand(
+                name=name,
+                linear=layer_spec(args.get("linear")),
+                moe=layer_spec(args.get("moe")),
+                deferred=name in deferred,
+            )
+        )
+    return shorthands
+
+
+def render_shorthands(
+    shorthands: list[Shorthand],
+    schemes: list[Scheme],
+    allow_lists: dict[str, set[str] | None],
+) -> str:
+    weight_names: dict[QuantKeySpec, str] = {}
+    for scheme in schemes:
+        key = scheme.weight_key or scheme.key
+        if key is not None:
+            weight_names.setdefault(key, scheme.name)
+
+    def cell(spec: LayerSpec | None) -> str:
+        if spec is None:
+            return "–"
+        if spec.weight is None:
+            text = _code(spec.weight_source)
+        elif spec.weight in weight_names:
+            text = _code(weight_names[spec.weight])
+        else:
+            text = _key_text(spec.weight)
+        if spec.hadamard_size is not None:
+            text += f" with a {spec.hadamard_size}-wide Hadamard rotation"
+        return text
+
+    rows = [
+        [
+            _code(shorthand.name),
+            cell(shorthand.linear),
+            cell(shorthand.moe),
+            _accepted_on([shorthand.name], allow_lists),
+        ]
+        for shorthand in shorthands
+    ]
+    table = _table(["Name", "Linear weights", "MoE weights", "Platforms"], rows)
+    deferred = [_code(s.name) for s in shorthands if s.deferred]
+    if not deferred:
+        return table
+    return (
+        f"{table}\n\n"
+        f"Also a method name: {', '.join(deferred)}. On a checkpoint that is "
+        "already quantized, these select the method of that name instead."
+    )
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Method:
+    """Method names that share one `QuantizationConfig` class."""
+
+    config: str
+    names: list[str]
+
+
+def parse_methods() -> tuple[list[Method], set[str]]:
+    """Return the methods and the deprecated method names."""
+    source = Source(QUANT_METHODS_FILE)
+    deprecated = set(
+        source.strings(
+            "DEPRECATED_QUANTIZATION_METHODS",
+            source.require("DEPRECATED_QUANTIZATION_METHODS"),
+        )
+    )
+    function = next(
+        (
+            node
+            for node in source.tree.body
+            if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef)
+            and node.name == "get_quantization_config"
+        ),
+        None,
+    )
+    if function is None:
+        raise source.error("get_quantization_config not found")
+
+    # Classes behind local variables (`deepseek_config = ...`) and import aliases.
+    # A variable assigned per platform is shown by class name only: the two
+    # `DeepseekV4FP8Config` classes of `deepseek_v4` and `deepseek_v41` are one row.
+    variables: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+    aliases: dict[str, str] = {}
+    table: ast.expr | None = None
+    for node in ast.walk(function):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
+            aliases.update({a.asname: a.name for a in node.names if a.asname})
+            continue
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and len(node.targets) == 1:
+            target, value = node.targets[0], node.value
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.AnnAssign) and node.value is not None:
+            target, value = node.target, node.value
+        else:
+            continue
+        if not isinstance(target, ast.Name):
+            continue
+        if target.id == "method_to_config":
+            table = value
+        elif isinstance(value, ast.Name):
+            variables.setdefault(target.id, []).append(value.id)
+    if table is None:
+        raise source.error("method_to_config not found in get_quantization_config")
+
+    by_config: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+    for name, value in source.dict_items("method_to_config", table):
+        symbol = _short(value)
+        classes = {aliases.get(c, c) for c in variables.get(symbol, [symbol])}
+        by_config.setdefault(" / ".join(sorted(classes)), []).append(name)
+    methods = [Method(config, names) for config, names in by_config.items()]
+    return methods, deprecated
+
+
+def render_methods(
+    methods: list[Method], deprecated: set[str], allow_lists: dict[str, set[str] | None]
+) -> str:
+    rows = []
+    for method in methods:
+        names = [
+            _code(name) + (" (deprecated)" if name in deprecated else "")
+            for name in method.names
+        ]
+        page = CONFIG_DOCS.get(method.config)
+        rows.append(
+            [
+                ", ".join(names),
+                _code(method.config),
+                _accepted_on(method.names, allow_lists),
+                f"[Guide]({page})" if page else "–",
+            ]
+        )
+    return _table(["Names", "Implementation", "Platforms", "Guide"], rows)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Linear kernels
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class LinearFamily:
+    """One linear kernel registry: kernels per platform, in priority order."""
+
+    registry: str
+    # Keys of `linear_backend_per_quant` read by the selector of this registry.
+    quant_keys: list[str]
+    kernels: dict[str, list[str]]
+
+    @property
+    def title(self) -> str:
+        return LINEAR_FAMILY_TITLES.get(self.registry) or _code(self.registry)
+
+
+def _string_choices(node: ast.expr | None) -> list[str]:
+    """The strings of a literal, or of both branches of a conditional of
+    literals. Any other expression gives none."""
+    if isinstance(node, ast.IfExp):
+        body, orelse = _string_choices(node.body), _string_choices(node.orelse)
+        return body + orelse if body and orelse else []
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, str):
+        return [node.value]
+    return []
+
+
+def _per_quant_keys(tree: ast.Module, registries: set[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
+    """Map each registry to the `quantization=` keys its selector passes.
+
+    A selector names its key as a string literal in a `quantization=` argument,
+    directly or through a local variable, either in the call that receives the
+    registry or elsewhere in a function that uses a single registry.
+    """
+    keys: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+    for function in tree.body:
+        if not isinstance(function, ast.FunctionDef):
+            continue
+        # Locals that are only ever assigned string literals.
+        local: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+        used: list[str] = []
+        for node in ast.walk(function):
+            if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and len(node.targets) == 1:
+                target = node.targets[0]
+                if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
+                    choices = _string_choices(node.value)
+                    known = local.setdefault(target.id, choices)
+                    local[target.id] = known + choices if known and choices else []
+            elif isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id in registries:
+                if node.id not in used:
+                    used.append(node.id)
+        for call in ast.walk(function):
+            if not isinstance(call, ast.Call):
+                continue
+            value = next(
+                (kw.value for kw in call.keywords if kw.arg == "quantization"), None
+            )
+            if isinstance(value, ast.Name):
+                found = local.get(value.id, [])
+            else:
+                found = _string_choices(value)
+            in_call = [
+                node.id
+                for node in ast.walk(call)
+                if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id in registries
+            ]
+            for registry in in_call or (used if len(used) == 1 else []):
+                merged = keys.setdefault(registry, [])
+                merged.extend(key for key in found if key not in merged)
+    return keys
+
+
+def parse_linear_families() -> tuple[list[LinearFamily], dict[str, list[str]]]:
+    """Return the kernel registries and the `--linear-backend` to kernels map."""
+    source = Source(LINEAR_KERNELS_FILE)
+
+    # A registry is a module-level dict of `PlatformEnum` members to lists.
+    registries: dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]] = {}
+    for name, value in source.assigned.items():
+        if not isinstance(value, ast.Dict):
+            continue
+        is_platform = [
+            isinstance(key, ast.Attribute) and _short(key.value) == "PlatformEnum"
+            for key in value.keys
+        ]
+        if not any(is_platform):
+            continue
+        if not all(is_platform):
+            raise source.error(f"{name} has a key that is not a PlatformEnum member")
+        if not all(isinstance(v, ast.List | ast.Tuple | ast.Set) for v in value.values):
+            continue
+        per_platform: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+        for platform, kernels in zip(value.keys, value.values, strict=True):
+            assert isinstance(platform, ast.Attribute)
+            names = source.elements(f"{name}[{platform.attr}]", kernels)
+            if names:
+                label = PLATFORM_NAMES.get(platform.attr, platform.attr)
+                per_platform[label] = names
+        registries[name] = dict(
+            sorted(per_platform.items(), key=lambda item: _platform_sort_key(item[0]))
+        )
+    if not registries:
+        raise source.error("no kernel registry keyed by PlatformEnum found")
+
+    backends = {
+        backend: source.elements(f"_LINEAR_BACKEND_KERNEL_MAP[{backend!r}]", kernels)
+        for backend, kernels in source.dict_items(
+            "_LINEAR_BACKEND_KERNEL_MAP", source.require("_LINEAR_BACKEND_KERNEL_MAP")
+        )
+    }
+
+    quant_keys = _per_quant_keys(source.tree, set(registries))
+    families = [
+        LinearFamily(name, quant_keys.get(name, []), kernels)
+        for name, kernels in registries.items()
+        if kernels
+    ]
+    return families, backends
+
+
+def render_linear_backends(
+    families: list[LinearFamily], backends: dict[str, list[str]]
+) -> str:
+    rows = []
+    for backend, kernels in backends.items():
+        covered = [
+            family
+            for family in families
+            if any(k in kernels for ks in family.kernels.values() for k in ks)
+        ]
+        platforms = sorted(
+            {
+                platform
+                for family in covered
+                for platform, ks in family.kernels.items()
+                if any(k in kernels for k in ks)
+            },
+            key=_platform_sort_key,
+        )
+        rows.append(
+            [
+                _code(backend),
+                ", ".join(platforms) or "–",
+                ", ".join(family.title for family in covered) or "–",
+            ]
+        )
+    return _table(["Backend", "Platforms", "Quantization types"], rows)
+
+
+def render_linear_families(families: list[LinearFamily]) -> str:
+    rows = [
+        [
+            family.title,
+            ", ".join(_code(key) for key in family.quant_keys) or "–",
+            ", ".join(family.kernels),
+        ]
+        for family in families
+    ]
+    return _table(
+        ["Quantization type", "`linear_backend_per_quant` key", "Platforms"], rows
+    )
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Entry point
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def build_blocks() -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
+    """Build the generated blocks per page, keyed by their `gen:` marker name."""
+    keys = QuantKeys()
+    schemes = parse_schemes(keys)
+    shorthands = parse_shorthands(keys)
+    allow_lists = parse_platform_allow_lists()
+    methods, deprecated = parse_methods()
+    families, backends = parse_linear_families()
+    return {
+        FORMATS_PAGE: {
+            "quantization-methods": render_methods(methods, deprecated, allow_lists),
+            "quantization-shorthands": render_shorthands(
+                shorthands, schemes, allow_lists
+            ),
+            "quantization-schemes": render_schemes(schemes),
+        },
+        KERNELS_PAGE: {
+            "linear-backends": render_linear_backends(families, backends),
+            "linear-families": render_linear_families(families),
+        },
+    }
+
+
+# mkdocs-gen-files runs this file with `runpy.run_path`.
+if __name__ == "<run_path>":
+    logger.info("Generating quantization documentation tables")
+    for page, blocks in build_blocks().items():
+        fill_markers(page, blocks)

         - docs/mkdocs/gen_files/generate_metrics.py

 NixlConnector is a high-performance KV cache transfer connector for vLLM's disaggregated prefilling feature. It provides fully asynchronous send/receive operations using the NIXL library for efficient cross-process KV cache transfer.
 
+`NixlPullConnector` is the canonical name for the pull connector; `NixlConnector` remains an alias, including inside `MultiConnector`. Both names use the same configuration checks and defaults.
+
 For feature compatibility details (supported model architectures, TP configurations, and feature interactions), see the [NixlConnector Compatibility Matrix](nixl_connector_compatibility.md).
 
 ## Prerequisites

   --decoder-ports 8200
 ```
 
+### Decode context parallelism
+
+NIXL pull transfers with `--decode-context-parallel-size` greater than 1 require an MLA model. When `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` is omitted, vLLM resolves it from the global KV cache groups before profiling. Explicit values are preserved and must divide the cache block size without exceeding it. For a block size of 16, explicit values of 1 and 8 are valid; 3 and 32 are rejected under either connector name.
+
 ## Environment Variables
 
 - `VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT`: Port for NIXL handshake communication

+    # Two 40-token chunks plus a lookahead slot: blocks below

+class DFlashSlidingWindowManager(SlidingWindowManager):
+    """Regular-attention sliding-window drafter KV read only near the end.
+
+    DFlash/DSpark context KV is a per-position projection of the target's
+    hidden states, and draft attention runs only past the last target token.
+    An allocation, including a KV-connector load's, therefore backs only the
+    blocks a draft step can read, those from `num_tokens_main_model -
+    tail_tokens` on; lower blocks are null, so a long prefill chunk holds one
+    tail rather than the whole chunk. The tail's margin over the window covers
+    in-flight drafts that may be rejected.
+
+    Frees and hits see no drafts in flight, so they use the window like plain
+    sliding window. A prefix hit at `h` for a request of `L` tokens needs
+    cached blocks only in `[L - sliding_window + 1, h)`: the drafter reads
+    only past the last target token, and everything from `h` on is
+    recomputed.
+    """
+
+    @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+    class Params(SlidingWindowManager.Params):
+        num_speculative_tokens: int = 0
+        """Drafts each step verifies; `T` counts them before acceptance."""
+        max_in_flight_steps: int = 1
+        num_lookahead_tokens: int = 0
+        """Slots each allocation backs past its target tokens for the drafts."""
+
+        @property
+        def tail_tokens(self) -> int:
+            """Tokens below `T` a draft step can still read: the window, plus
+            the drafts each in-flight step counts in `T` and may reject."""
+            return (
+                self.sliding_window
+                + self.num_speculative_tokens * self.max_in_flight_steps
+            )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def max_admission_blocks(
+        cls,
+        config: ManagerConfig,
+        block_size: int,
+        max_in_flight_tokens: int,
+        max_model_len: int,
+    ) -> int | None:
+        # The processed prefix's window plus one tail per in-flight step: steps
+        # back only their own trailing tail, however long their chunk. Both
+        # bounds cover the lookahead slots past the last allocation's tokens.
+        params = config.params
+        assert isinstance(params, DFlashSlidingWindowManager.Params)
+        window_blocks = super().max_admission_blocks(
+            config,
+            block_size,
+            max_in_flight_tokens + params.num_lookahead_tokens,
+            max_model_len,
+        )
+        assert window_blocks is not None
+        tail_blocks = (
+            cdiv(
+                params.tail_tokens
+                + params.extra_retained_tokens
+                + params.num_lookahead_tokens,
+                block_size,

+            + 1

+    if (

+def _check_glm52_planned_call(
+    capability: tuple[int, int],
+    n: int,
+    k: int,
+    num_tokens: int,
+    backend: str,
+    cuda_graph: bool,
+) -> None:
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    x = torch.randn(num_tokens, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    weight = torch.randn(n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == capability:
+        plan = _glm52_device_plan(weight, num_tokens, backend)
+    else:
+        # Same architecture family: run that table's row directly.
+        plan = dict(GLM_GPU_TABLES)[capability][(n, k)].build_plan()
+        assert plan[num_tokens][0] == backend
+
+    output = glm52_gemm.run_glm52_plan(plan, x, weight)
+    if cuda_graph:
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            output = glm52_gemm.run_glm52_plan(plan, x, weight)

+        x.normal_()
+        graph.replay()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+

   letters.
 - When each request carries one question over a state that changes from
   request to request, `--disable-prefix-caching` lowers latency.
+
+### Mammoth-1 and Elephant-1
+
+Base Labs [`baselabs/mammoth-1`](https://huggingface.co/baselabs/mammoth-1)
+and [`baselabs/elephant-1`](https://huggingface.co/baselabs/elephant-1) are
+Qwen3.5 checkpoints whose `modeling_overrides` select `Qwen3_5ForSlotDecision`.
+
+```bash
+vllm serve baselabs/mammoth-1
+```
+
+- The full attention layers read the shared prefix and the question as two
+  bidirectional blocks, and each prompt is prefilled in one step. Chunked
+  prefill is therefore off for every request on the server, a
+  `--max-num-batched-tokens` below `--max-model-len` is raised to it, and a
+  smaller `--max-num-scheduled-tokens` is refused. `--max-model-len` defaults
+  to the trained 16,384 tokens.
+- Prefix caching (on by default) prefills the shared prefix once per decision
+  request instead of once per question. It needs FlashInfer's GatedDeltaNet
+  prefill (Hopper, or Blackwell with CUDA 13) and is turned off with other
+  backends.
+- A `choice` can have up to 255 options, labeled `A` to `Z` and then with
+  two-letter labels in the prompt. Media inputs return 400.
+- Only the `TRITON_ATTN` attention backend is supported, and it is selected
+  automatically. KV transfer connectors, `--kv-offloading-size`, speculative
+  decoding, context parallelism, micro-batching, `--prefix-match-unit` and
+  `--scheduler-cls` are refused.
+- `instructions` returns 400, as does any `chat_template_kwargs` other than
+  `{"enable_thinking": false}`. `/v1/decisions` reads every question as a
+  choice and returns 400 for score levels with the same label.

+STATE = {

+}
+QUESTIONS = {

+    "team": {

+        "instructions": "Which team should handle this?",
+        "criteria": {"billing": "charges", "technical": "bugs", "sales": "pricing"},
+    },
+    "mood": {
+        "type": "score",
+        "instructions": "How frustrated is the customer?",
+        "criteria": ["calm", "irritated", "angry"],
+    },
+}
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def server(tmp_path_factory):
+    checkpoint = str(tmp_path_factory.mktemp("slot-decision"))
+    build_tiny_checkpoint(checkpoint)
+    args = [
+        "--dtype",
+        "bfloat16",
+        "--served-model-name",
+        MODEL_NAME,
+        "--max-model-len",
+        "2048",
+        "--max-num-seqs",
+        "8",
+        "--enforce-eager",
+        "--gpu-memory-utilization",
+        "0.3",

+    ]
+    with RemoteOpenAIServer(checkpoint, args) as remote_server:
+        yield remote_server
+
+
+def systemone(server, **body):
+    return requests.post(

+    )
+
+
+def check_probabilities(probabilities: dict[str, float], names: set[str]) -> None:
+    assert set(probabilities) == names
+    assert all(0.0 <= p <= 1.0 for p in probabilities.values())

+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Qwen3_5ForSlotDecision's block attention against the transformers block mask,
+on a random four-layer model built from BLOCK_ATTN_BASE."""
+
+import os
+from functools import partial
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from tests.models.test_qwen3_5_slot import OVERRIDES
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+BASE = os.environ.get("BLOCK_ATTN_BASE", "baselabs/elephant-1")
+NUM_SCORED = 256
+# bf16 vLLM against an fp32 reference.
+ATOL = 0.1
+
+pytestmark = [
+    pytest.mark.hybrid_model,
+    pytest.mark.skipif(
+        not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="block attention needs a CUDA GPU"
+    ),
+]
+
+
+def build_tiny_checkpoint(path: str) -> None:
+    from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoProcessor, Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration
+
+    config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(BASE)
+    config.text_config.update({
+        "hidden_size": 256, "intermediate_size": 512, "num_hidden_layers": 4,
+        "layer_types": ["linear_attention", "full_attention"] * 2,
+        "num_attention_heads": 4, "num_key_value_heads": 2,
+        "linear_num_key_heads": 2, "linear_num_value_heads": 2,
+        "mtp_num_hidden_layers": 0, "dtype": "float32",
+    })  # fmt: skip
+    config.vision_config.update({
+        "depth": 1, "hidden_size": 64, "num_heads": 2, "intermediate_size": 128,
+        "out_hidden_size": 256,
+    })  # fmt: skip
+    config.modeling_overrides = OVERRIDES
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    model = Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration(config).to(torch.float32)
+    # Sharper weights and stronger attention values/outputs make the mask move
+    # the last token's logits well above bf16 noise.
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
+            if param.dim() > 1:
+                strong = "self_attn.v_proj" in name or "self_attn.o_proj" in name
+                param.normal_(0.0, 0.32 if strong else 0.08)
+    model.save_pretrained(path)
+    AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(BASE).save_pretrained(path)
+
+
+def hf_logprobs(path: str, prompts: dict, prefix_len: int) -> list[dict]:
+    """Last-position logprobs over the first NUM_SCORED tokens of each prompt,
+    with the prefix and the rest as two blocks, then causal."""
+    from transformers import Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration
+    from transformers.models.qwen3_5 import modeling_qwen3_5 as hf
+
+    model = Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
+        path, dtype=torch.float32, attn_implementation="sdpa"
+    ).to("cuda")
+    mask = hf.create_causal_mask
+
+    def run(prompt: list[int], blocked: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
+        ids = (torch.arange(len(prompt), device="cuda") >= prefix_len).long()[None]
+        patched = partial(mask, block_sequence_ids=ids if blocked else None)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(hf, "create_causal_mask", patched)
+        with torch.inference_mode():
+            logits = model(input_ids=torch.tensor([prompt], device="cuda")).logits
+        return torch.log_softmax(logits[0, -1].float(), -1)[:NUM_SCORED].cpu()
+
+    with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as monkeypatch:
+        return [{q: run(p, b) for q, p in prompts.items()} for b in (True, False)]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enforce_eager", [True, False])
+def test_block_attention_matches_transformers(vllm_runner, tmp_path, enforce_eager):
+    from vllm import SamplingParams
+    from vllm.inputs import TokensPrompt
+
+    checkpoint = str(tmp_path)
+    build_tiny_checkpoint(checkpoint)
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(1)
+
+    def tokens(n: int) -> list[int]:
+        return torch.randint(1000, 100000, (n,), generator=g).tolist()
+
+    # A long shared prefix, then three questions.
+    prefix = tokens(700)
+    shared = tokens(40)
+    questions = {
+        "q0": prefix + tokens(90),
+        "q1": prefix + shared + tokens(50),
+        "q2": prefix + shared + tokens(50),
+    }
+    p = len(prefix)
+    expected, causal = hf_logprobs(checkpoint, questions, p)
+    torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
+    for q in questions:
+        # The mask must matter, or the comparison proves nothing.
+        assert (causal[q] - expected[q]).abs().max() > 5 * ATOL, q
+
+    def params(prefix_len: int | None) -> SamplingParams:
+        return SamplingParams(
+            max_tokens=1,
+            temperature=0.0,
+            logprob_token_ids=list(range(NUM_SCORED)),
+            extra_args=None if prefix_len is None else {"prefix_lm_len": prefix_len},
+        )
+
+    # Room for every prompt in one step, so the reads share a batch.
+    with vllm_runner(
+        checkpoint,
+        dtype="bfloat16",
+        max_model_len=2048,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=4096,
+        enable_prefix_caching=True,
+        enforce_eager=enforce_eager,
+        gpu_memory_utilization=0.4,
+        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0, "video": 0},
+    ) as runner:
+        llm = runner.llm
+        vllm_config = llm.llm_engine.vllm_config
+        assert vllm_config.model_config.head_dtype == torch.float32
+        # Prefix caching stays on with FlashInfer's GDN prefill only.
+        prefix_caching = vllm_config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching
+        if prefix_caching:
+            scheduler_cls = vllm_config.scheduler_config.scheduler_cls
+            assert scheduler_cls.startswith("vllm.v1.core.sched.prefix_lm_scheduler.")
+
+        # The three questions with their blocks, then q0 without a prefix length,
+        # which is read causally.
+        outputs = llm.generate(
+            [TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=questions[q]) for q in [*questions, "q0"]],
+            [params(p)] * len(questions) + [params(None)],
+            use_tqdm=False,
+        )
+        references = [*expected.values(), causal["q0"]]
+
+        def check(name: str, out, reference) -> None:
+            logprobs = out.outputs[0].logprobs[0]
+            got = torch.tensor([logprobs[t].logprob for t in range(NUM_SCORED)])
+            error = (got - reference).abs().max().item()
+            assert error < ATOL, (name, error)
+
+        for args in zip([*questions, "q0 causal"], outputs, references):
+            check(*args)
+
+        if not prefix_caching:
+            return
+        # The prefix alone, as the strategy's warm-up sends it. The questions
+        # then reuse its cache, and never past it: q1 and q2 share 40 more
+        # tokens, and q2 comes twice.
+        llm.generate(TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=prefix), params(p), use_tqdm=False)
+        for name in ("q1", "q2", "q2"):
+            (out,) = llm.generate(
+                TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=questions[name]),
+                params(p),
+                use_tqdm=False,
+            )
+            check(f"{name} cached", out, expected[name])
+            assert 0 < (out.num_cached_tokens or 0) <= p, out.num_cached_tokens

+def make_request(req_id, prompt, prefix_len, salt="own", resumable=False):
+    """A PrefixLM request with the strategy's salt, or causal if prefix_len is None."""
+    if salt == "own":
+        salt = None if prefix_len is None else prefix_lm_salt(prompt[:prefix_len], None)
+    extra_args = None if prefix_len is None else {PREFIX_LM_LEN: prefix_len}
+    params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, extra_args=extra_args)
+    params.update_from_generation_config({}, EOS_TOKEN_ID)
+    init_none_hash(sha256)
+    return Request(
+        request_id=req_id,
+        prompt_token_ids=prompt,
+        sampling_params=params,
+        pooling_params=None,
+        cache_salt=salt,
+        resumable=resumable,
+        block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(16, sha256),
+    )

+    """Add the requests and run one step. Returns the cached and scheduled
+    tokens of each new request."""
+    for request in requests:
+        scheduler.add_request(request)
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    ids = list(output.num_scheduled_tokens)
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        output,
+        ModelRunnerOutput(ids, [[0]] * len(ids)),
+    )
+    return {
+        r.req_id: (r.num_computed_tokens, output.num_scheduled_tokens[r.req_id])
+        for r in output.scheduled_new_reqs

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The fixed prompt of slot-readout decision models, byte for byte as trained."""
+
+import json
+from typing import Any
+
+from .question_types import LABELS
+
+SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
+    "Apply the question to the state. Choose exactly one of the listed options. "
+    "Respond with only its uppercase letter, with no explanation or reasoning."
+)
+#: Two-letter labels that are not one token in the Qwen3.5 vocabulary.
+_NOT_ONE_TOKEN = frozenset({
+    "BQ", "BZ", "CJ", "CQ", "CZ", "DQ", "DZ", "EJ", "EY", "FJ", "FQ", "FV", "FZ",
+    "GJ", "GK", "GQ", "GZ", "HJ", "IY", "JF", "JG", "JH", "JL", "JN", "JQ",
+})  # fmt: skip
+_PAIRS = tuple(a + b for a in LABELS for b in LABELS if a + b not in _NOT_ONE_TOKEN)
+#: Slot i labels option i: A to Z, then the two-letter labels in order.
+SLOT_LABELS = LABELS + _PAIRS[: 256 - len(LABELS)]
+DEFAULT_INSTRUCTIONS = {
+    "choice": "Which option applies to the state?",
+    "noul": "Is the statement true, or is the answer to the question yes?",
+    "score": "Which level describes the state?",
+}
+NOUL_DEFAULTS = {
+    "true": "the statement is true / the answer is yes",
+    "false": "the statement is false / the answer is no",
+}
+#: Placed where a suffix goes to find where the shared prefix ends.
+PREFIX_MARK = "QEV_PREFIX_MARK"
+
+
+def render_state(value: Any, strip: bool = False) -> str:
+    """Strings as they are (stripped with `strip`), others as indented JSON."""
+    if value is None:
+        return ""
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        return value.strip() if strip else value
+    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
+
+
+def render_suffix(type_name: str, instructions: Any, criteria: Any) -> str:
+    """The question, its options under slot labels and the answer line."""
+    if type_name == "noul":
+        criteria = criteria or {}
+        names = ["yes", "no"]
+        descriptions = [
+            d if criteria.get(k) is None else criteria[k]
+            for k, d in NOUL_DEFAULTS.items()
+        ]
+    elif type_name == "choice":
+        names, descriptions = list(criteria), list(criteria.values())
+    else:
+        names, descriptions = [f"level {i}" for i in range(len(criteria))], criteria
+    lines = []
+    for label, name, desc in zip(SLOT_LABELS, names, descriptions):
+        text = render_state(desc, strip=True)
+        lines.append(f"{label}. {name}: {text}" if text else f"{label}. {name}")
+    header = "Rate the state:" if type_name == "score" else "Question:"
+    question = render_state(instructions, strip=True) or DEFAULT_INSTRUCTIONS[type_name]
+    kind = "letter" if len(names) <= len(LABELS) else "label"
+    options, labels = "\n".join(lines), ", ".join(SLOT_LABELS[: len(names)])
+    return (
+        f"{header} {question}\n\nOptions:\n{options}\n\n"
+        f"Answer with one {kind}: {labels}."
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Prefix caching for PrefixLM requests, which send their prefix length in
+`extra_args["prefix_lm_len"]`: salts each prefix's blocks by its digest, as the KV
+of every prefix token depends on the whole prefix, and caps hits at the prefix.
+The model turns chunked prefill off, so the rest of the prompt is prefilled in
+one step."""
+
+import copy
+import hashlib
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_manager import KVCacheBlocks
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.async_scheduler import AsyncScheduler
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler import Scheduler
+from vllm.v1.request import Request
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+PREFIX_LM_LEN = "prefix_lm_len"
+"""`SamplingParams.extra_args` key of the length of a prompt's PrefixLM prefix."""
+
+PREFIX_LM_SALT = "prefix-lm:"
+"""Start of the `cache_salt` of every PrefixLM request, and of no other."""
+
+
+def prefix_lm_len(
+    params: SamplingParams | None, prompt_token_ids: Sequence[int] | None
+) -> int | None:
+    """The valid PrefixLM prefix length a request sends, else None."""
+    extra_args = params.extra_args if params is not None else None
+    prefix_len = extra_args.get(PREFIX_LM_LEN) if extra_args else None
+    if (
+        type(prefix_len) is int
+        and prompt_token_ids is not None
+        and 0 < prefix_len <= len(prompt_token_ids)
+    ):
+        return prefix_len
+    return None
+
+
+def prefix_lm_salt(prefix_token_ids: Sequence[int], cache_salt: str | None) -> str:
+    """PrefixLM `cache_salt`: namespace, prefix digest, then the caller's salt."""
+    digest = hashlib.sha256(
+        np.asarray(prefix_token_ids, dtype="<i8").tobytes()
+    ).hexdigest()
+    salt = PREFIX_LM_SALT + digest
+    return f"{salt}:{cache_salt}" if cache_salt else salt
+
+
+def _request_prefix_lm_len(request: Request) -> int | None:
+    return prefix_lm_len(request.sampling_params, request.prompt_token_ids)
+
+
+class PrefixLMScheduler(Scheduler):
+    def __new__(cls, *args, **kwargs):
+        # Model hooks pick this class before async scheduling is decided, so
+        # build the async twin here when the engine runs async.
+        vllm_config = kwargs["vllm_config"] if "vllm_config" in kwargs else args[0]
+        if cls is PrefixLMScheduler and vllm_config.scheduler_config.async_scheduling:
+            cls = PrefixLMAsyncScheduler
+        return super().__new__(cls)
+
+    def add_request(self, request: Request) -> None:
+        params = request.sampling_params
+        if (
+            (request.resumable or request.mm_features)
+            and params is not None
+            and PREFIX_LM_LEN in (params.extra_args or {})
+        ):
+            # Later inputs and encoder budgets can cut such a prompt short.
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "Requests with streamed or multimodal inputs ignore %s",
+                PREFIX_LM_LEN,
+            )
+            request.sampling_params = params = copy.copy(params)
+            params.extra_args = dict(params.extra_args or {})
+            del params.extra_args[PREFIX_LM_LEN]
+        # A streaming update re-adds an existing request.
+        if request.request_id not in self.requests:
+            self._salt_by_kind(request)
+        super().add_request(request)
+
+    def _salt_by_kind(self, request: Request) -> None:
+        """Salt PrefixLM requests by prefix; keep causal requests out."""
+        prefix_len = _request_prefix_lm_len(request)
+        salt = request.cache_salt
+        if prefix_len is None:
+            if not (salt and salt.startswith(PREFIX_LM_SALT)):
+                return
+            salt = f"causal:{salt}"
+        else:
+            assert request.prompt_token_ids is not None
+            own = prefix_lm_salt(request.prompt_token_ids[:prefix_len], None)
+            if salt == own or (salt and salt.startswith(f"{own}:")):
+                return
+            salt = f"{own}:{salt}" if salt else own
+        request.cache_salt = salt
+        request.block_hashes.clear()
+        request.update_block_hashes()
+
+    def _get_local_prefix_cache_hit(
+        self, request: Request, max_cache_hit_length: int | None = None
+    ) -> tuple[KVCacheBlocks, int, int, bool]:
+        prefix_len = _request_prefix_lm_len(request)
+        if prefix_len is None:
+            return super()._get_local_prefix_cache_hit(request, max_cache_hit_length)
+        # KV past the prefix depends on the rest of the prompt, and a hit keeps
+        # the last prompt token to compute.
+        cap = min(prefix_len, request.num_tokens - 1)
+        if max_cache_hit_length is not None:
+            cap = min(cap, max_cache_hit_length)
+        blocks, num_tokens, _, diverged = super()._get_local_prefix_cache_hit(
+            request, cap
+        )
+        # No shared-prefix junction: Mamba alignment would end a step there,
+        # inside the prefix.
+        return blocks, num_tokens, 0, diverged
+
+
+class PrefixLMAsyncScheduler(PrefixLMScheduler, AsyncScheduler): ...
